items.claim: Gujarat Samachar reported that 634 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names were filed in two polling booths of Danilimda (booths 193 and 194) by two persons it described as BJP workers, and that a complaint was registered at Isanpur police station.
items.quote: In the Danilimda assembly constituency, two BJP workers have reportedly submitted a total of 634 Form-7 applications seeking deletion of voter names. ... A complaint in this regard has been registered at Isanpur Police Station.
items.note: The article names the two filers and gives a per-booth split (396 at booth 193, 238 at booth 194); names omitted here under the site's rule. 'Reportedly' is the paper's word. No official response is reported. No outcome of the police complaint was found. The quote joins two sentences of the article with an ellipsis.

items.claim: Gujarat Samachar reported a dispute over attempts to remove from the roll residents left without homes by the Chandola Lake demolitions, alleging that their lack of residential documents was being used to seek deletion.
items.quote: It is alleged that the lack of residential documents among these homeless residents is now being used to seek deletion of their names from the electoral rolls.
items.note: Allegation as reported; the article does not say who alleged it. Same article reports opposition groups planned representations to the State Election Commission and possible court action; no follow-up found.

items.claim: Chandola Lake lies in Danilimda, and the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation demolished more than 10,000 structures around it in two phases, on 29 April and 20 May 2025, months before the SIR began.
items.quote: the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) demolished over 10,000 illegal structures around Chandola Lake in Danilimda, reclaiming approximately 4 lakh square meters of public land. Conducted in two phases on 29 April and 20 May, the operation aimed to restore the ecological integrity of the lake
items.note: Place profile only. The article also reports the state's national-security framing and detentions; none of that is used here, and nothing here should be read as a statement about anyone's citizenship. The article reports rents rising in Danilimda and Isanpur as displaced families looked for homes.

items.claim: Municipal election rolls show the Danilimda ward, which includes the Chandola Lake area, fell by 19,346 registered voters between 2021 and 2026; the paper says the fall does not by itself show how many names the SIR deleted.
items.quote: In Danilimda, which includes the Chandola Lake area, the electorate fell by 19,346, from 98,040 to 78,694. ... Notably, the decline in registered voters, however, does not by itself establish how many names were deleted during the SIR or how many residents were displaced by demolitions.
items.note: This is the AMC ward, not assembly constituency 54. The article's own table prints the 2026 figure as 76,940, which does not match 98,040 less 19,346 (78,694); the text figure is arithmetically consistent. Article also gives the ECI's special registration camps on 11, 18 and 25 October and 1 November 2026 (Form 6 at polling stations).

items.claim: The Ahmedabad unit of the Congress said many demolition drives were targeted constituency-wise and ward-wise and that it had worked to address voter deletions over the past year.
items.quote: Ahmedabad Congress president Sonal Patel said the party had to make considerable efforts to address voter deletions in this past year. She also mentioned that many of the drives were targeted constituency-wise and ward-wise.
items.note: Party claim, attribute to the Congress (Ahmedabad unit). The quote contains the office-holder's name as printed; on the site, attribute to the party. No response from the AMC or the BJP is reported in the article.

items.claim: A minority rights group's letter to Gujarat's Chief Electoral Officer said residents displaced from Chandola Lake were given special camps to complete their forms and that their names appear in the draft roll, contrasting them with displaced residents of a settlement in Bapunagar.
items.quote: The MCC further alleges discrimination, pointing out that residents of Chandola Lake—whose houses were also demolished—were provided special camps to complete voter documentation and their names appear in the current draft rolls.
items.outlet: Counterview (report of the Minority Coordination Committee Gujarat's letter to the CEO dated 17 January 2026)
items.note: This cuts against the idea that Chandola residents were simply dropped at the draft stage; it is the organisation's statement, not an official one. No CEO or DEO confirmation of special camps for Chandola residents was found. The letter itself was not found online; the report was read.

items.claim: The Wire reported a second large demolition, at Isanpur lake in November 2025, during the SIR enumeration period, and an RTI activist's view that demolitions during the revision cost residents their entries.
items.quote: In November 2025, the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) along with police launched a mega demolition drive to clear illegal encroachments at Ahmedabad’s Isanpur lake. ... “The demolition could have been delayed, it was not necessary to be conducted during the SIR. Their names were lost from lists”
items.outlet: The Wire (republished by Vibes of India)
items.note: Read via the Vibes of India republication (https://www.vibesofindia.com/gujarat-should-house-demolitions-lead-to-sir-deletions-civil-society-activists-say-they-are/) because thewire.in did not render. The activist is named in the article; described here by role. Whether Isanpur lake falls in AC 54 Danilimda was not confirmed from a source. The article says ECI gave no guidelines on demolitions during the SIR; that is the activist's statement.

items.claim: After the final roll of 17 February 2026, Gujarat did not publish the names and reasons for deletions made after the draft, though it had published such lists with the draft; a minority rights group asked the Commission to publish them.
items.quote: કેટલાંક સંગઠનોનું કહેવું છે કે અંતિમ યાદીમાં કાપાયેલા મતદારોનાં નામ અને કારણોની વિગત જાહેર કરવામાં આવી નથી, જ્યારે ડ્રાફ્ટ યાદી સમયે આવી માહિતી ઉપલબ્ધ હતી.
items.date: 2026-02 (after the 17 February 2026 final roll; exact date not shown in the text read)
items.note: Translation of quote: 'Some organisations say the names and reasons of voters cut in the final list have not been published, whereas such information was available at the time of the draft list.' Relevant because Danilimda's 8,289 post-draft deletions have no published reason. Same article: Ahmedabad district about 47,000 deleted and 1,53,234 added between draft and final. Read from the full text returned by search; date to be confirmed on the page.

items.claim: Gujarat's election officials gave two very different statewide Form 7 counts two days apart, 9,88,621 on 29 January and 1,83,235 on 31 January 2026, and the CEO did not answer The Hindu's question about the gap.
items.quote: election officials said on January 29 that the SIR exercise had so far recorded 6.88 lakh applications for the addition of names and 9,88,621 Form 7 applications for deletion. However, contradicting this statement, the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer issued another release two days later, on January 31, stating that January 30 was the last day to submit claims and objections, with a total of just 1,83,235 Form 7 submissions.
items.note: Statewide context, no Danilimda figure. The article reports Congress and AAP allegations of bulk pre-typed Form 7s and the BJP state president's denial ('neither the party nor the government had any role'); attribute to parties if used. It reports a Form 7 episode in Ahmedabad's Gomtipur area, which is not Danilimda.

items.claim: The Gujarat High Court issued notice to the Election Commission and the state on two petitions seeking a special investigation team into allegedly illegal bulk Form 7 objections during the SIR, and listed the matter for 7 July 2026.
items.quote: They have claimed that as part of a "larger conspiracy" thousands of illegal objection applications under form-7 were filed seeking deletion of voters' names during the recently concluded Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the state. Justice Hemant Prachchhak issued notice on Friday while posting the matter for further hearing on July 7.
items.note: Statewide; the petitions concern Kodinar and Sidhpur, not Danilimda. Petitioners include Congress office-holders; attribute to petitioners or the party. No order text, case number or outcome of the 7 July hearing was found. BBC Gujarati (15 Feb 2026, https://www.bbc.com/gujarati/articles/c93j8j3e44no) also reports a 12 February petition by Congress leaders seeking compliance with the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

not_found: No CEO Gujarat or DEO Ahmedabad statement, release or table specific to Danilimda (AC 54) was found: no constituency count of Form 6 or Form 7 applications, notices, hearings, or reasons for the 8,289 deletions after the draft.
No published reason for Danilimda being the only Ahmedabad seat whose final roll is below its draft; the CEO published no list of names or reasons for post-draft deletions (BBC Gujarati, dan-08).

The site's own post-draft figures for Danilimda (5,214 added, 8,289 deleted, 2,10,342 final) come from the Gujarat Samachar graphic of 17 February 2026 already in data/gujarat/raw/ahmedabad_final_ac_press.csv; that graphic was not re-read for this file.
No outcome found for the Isanpur police station complaint over the 634 Form 7s (dan-01), and no ERO decision on those applications.
No court order or petition specific to Danilimda was found; the Gujarat High Court petitions found (dan-10) concern other constituencies.
No official confirmation of special SIR camps for Chandola Lake residents (asserted by MCC, dan-06).
No documented protest in Danilimda over the SIR was found. A BLO protest in Ahmedabad (Khokhra, 27 Nov 2025) is already in the site's disputes research and is not in Danilimda.
Could not confirm from a named source whether the Isanpur lake demolition site (Nov 2025) lies in AC 54.
The Danilimda MLA's Facebook post on false Form 7 objections (search result, Gujarati) could not be scraped (Facebook unsupported); not cited.
No figure was found for how many Danilimda electors were shifted, absent or dead at the draft stage beyond the site's own CEO tables.
